Chapter 8: Collateral Damage Jake slammed back into existence with a soundless scream, his lungs seizing around phantom fire. The air tore into him like barbed wire, too sharp, too dry, too fast — his mind stuttered around his senses in chaotic bursts of disorientation — uncoordinated limbs thrashing violently against the world around him. He clawed at his chest, the ground, whatever limbs or hands were near enough to catch. Anything to anchor himself. Anything to get out . Everything burned. His nerves lit up in jagged afterimages of torment, phantom electricity screaming down his spine and out through his limbs. No position gave relief. No movement lessened it. His mind stuttered and skidded across broken sensory input — sound and color and pressure flooding in all at once, none of it lining up, none of it making sense . A hundred fragments of reality all jammed into the same second. And something was touching him. Hands. Arms. Seemingly everywhere . Trying to hold him down. Voices, shouting, distant and warped like they were underwater. Jake erupted , flailing against the phantom restraints with every wild, adrenaline-drenched ounce of strength he had left. He couldn’t tell if he was hitting the floor or someone’s leg or a wall, but one of his fists caught something solid and some of the hands fell away, only to be replaced by even stronger ones. They hooked around his arms and shoulders, pulled him upright — someone braced behind him, locking him in place like a seatbelt. He had no balance, no leverage. His feet scrabbled uselessly across the ground. Everything was too much . Too loud, too bright. Light carved white-hot streaks across his vision. Sound hit in smeared vibrations, voices collapsing into meaningless noise. A scream caught in his throat as electricity still danced in phantom arcs along his spine. The arms locked across his chest didn’t budge — a steady pressure pinning him in place, anchoring him as he fought and flailed and finally... broke . Behind him, someone breathed slow and calm, exhaling soft rhythm into the crook of his neck, like trying to pace him down from the edge. A voice — low, familiar, more tone than any words he could recognize — murmured quiet nonsense against his ear. It didn’t matter what they were saying. The sound of it sliced through the screaming in his skull, dragging his mind back one fragile thread at a time. The fire in his chest slowed. The shaking dulled. Jake’s limbs sagged, twitching instead of thrashing, the force of his panic bleeding out in great gasping sobs that wracked his whole frame. His breath hitched again and again, caught between pain and grief and exhausted terror. The grip around him shifted, and he let it — let them pull him sideways, let his face be tucked against warm fabric and steady muscle, away from the worst of the light. The hands that had tried holding him down had softened into grounding touches and exploratory prods against pulse points and mostly healed burns. His mind swam. Ears roared. The adrenaline was gone but nothing coherent took its place — just static, floating somewhere below the surface of himself. He felt the world tip, just slightly, somewhere behind his ribs. His consciousness pitched downward, a wave folding in on itself — and Jake let it. Let it take him. Let the pain go. Let everything go. Soft murmurs stirred him back toward the surface — warm voices through the static, low and familiar. How long had he been out? Jake inhaled, wincing as the scent of burning wood and sweat flooded his senses. Campfire. Damp earth. Cloth soaked with adrenaline and blood. He blinked through the fog, squeezing his eyes shut against the light, body aching down to the bone. The camp. The other survivors. Safety . Pain still throbbed across his ribs, his arms, his spine — but it was distant now, dull. Already the Fog was doing its work, nibbling away at the worst of it. In a few trials, the memory of the pain would fade. Jake tried opening his eyes again and, through blurred static, caught on a blur of motion a short distance from the fire. Ace sat a little ways off, being gently interrogated by Dwight’s medkit. The man looked *rough *— one hell of a black eye blooming across his temple, sunglasses gone, and a shallow cut tracing just beneath his brow. He kept flinching as Dwight dabbed at him, muttering colorful commentary through the fussing. When he noticed Jake watching, Ace gave a crooked grin and a two-fingered salute — then winced again as Dwight swatted his hand away. Jake exhaled a weak breath that might’ve been a laugh if he had the energy. Right. That must’ve been who he hit. Something shifted against his back, and Jake glanced down to find a familiar scarred forearm wrapped around him, anchoring him to a battered shirt. David. He shifted slightly, only to realize he’d been curled against the man. Too tired to be embarrassed. Almost. Blinking away the haze, he spotted Claudette and Meg chatting quietly with Felix and Leon near the fire. Leon looked tired, his wrist tightly wrapped in layers of gauze. He was a little slouched in on himself, but alert, apparently in discussion over something. Meg caught his gaze and gave a tight smile. Jake let out a long breath and sagged against David’s side. They were OK. They made it out. “You back with us?” David’s voice was low and dry with a hint of amusement as he poked gently at Jake’s temple.
